title: The matching kind: which records are the same thing, pair by pair, with a record and its matches on one side, certified on copied bills and two real benchmarks
request: Phase 8 (the owner's pattern 4): a sixteenth kind; one row is a pair; exact links first, blocking, similarity features, nearest neighbours; split by entity; pair precision and recall; certified on the copied-bills trap and a real dataset.
plan: Map how a kind with its own machine is added (the ranking kind as the model), the retail replica's copied bills, and which real datasets exist.
Write the library: the split by entity first, blocking, features per field, models chosen on validation pairs, the holdout read once.
Wire the kind, its machine, its code export, the router and the certification; ask the owner for a real benchmark.
Certify on three replica seeds and two real datasets under the existing rule.

decisions.decision: The split is fixed by entity before any pair is formed: the known matches join records, and an entity goes whole to one side.
decisions.why: A copy learned from on one side and scored on the other would flatter every score.

decisions.decision: No real dataset was on the machine; the owner chose to download two public benchmarks (DBLP-ACM and Abt-Buy) and keep the two-real-dataset rule.
decisions.why: The plan's 'one real dataset' would have lowered the recipes' rule; two benchmarks meet it as written.

decisions.decision: The bills carry the plan's exact link, whether the cashier who sold a bill returned it, from the returns table.
decisions.why: A copy is always returned by its seller and an honest bill rarely; without it two of three seeds fell below the trap's bars.

decisions.decision: The router chooses matching only where a table of two identifiers and little else is shown.
decisions.why: It must never take a rare event or an anomaly problem that has no known pairs.

decisions.decision: The frozen sealed journey sets are checked against the fifteen kinds they were written for.
decisions.why: A set frozen before a kind existed cannot hold it; the new kind gets its own people later.

decisions.decision: A holdout record is paired with every record, not only with the holdout's.
decisions.why: A new bill is checked against every bill sold before; pairing it only with its own part flattered recall (the first run's 0.89 on the bills fell to 0.76).

change: dclab_core.matching (setup, candidates, features, validate, score, evaluate); dclab_rnd.kinds.matching (Matching, MatchingFields, MatchingMachine, the replica case with the return-by-seller link, real_cases); the code export's _matching; certify.run_kind and --kind; solutions' pairs_table precondition and matching approach; research/record-linkage; dclab-core 0.92.0.

findings.defect: Two of three replica seeds failed the copied-bills trap check.
findings.scenario: Seeds 1 and 2: pair F1 0.419 and 0.333, precision or recall under the bars, though the rule's count said certified.
findings.cause: Amount, time, store and items alone cannot tell a copy from an honest look-alike, which outnumber copies five to one.
findings.fix: The plan's exact link as a field: a return by the cashier who sold the bill.

findings.defect: The frozen sealed journey sets failed for a kind added after them.
findings.scenario: test_journeys asserted every set covers every kind.
findings.cause: The sets were checked against the live list of kinds.
findings.fix: Checked against the fifteen kinds they were written for, and those still exist.

findings.defect: The holdout's candidate pairs were formed only inside the holdout part.
findings.scenario: A holdout bill copied from a training bill was never paired with it, so the measured recall left out the copies a new record would be matched against.
findings.cause: candidates paired a part's records with the same part's records only.
findings.fix: SEES: validation records against training and validation, holdout records against every record, as a new record would be matched.

findings.defect: The router chose matching for problems with no table of known pairs.
findings.scenario: A rare-event brief with a related table of an id and a date ranked matching first.
findings.cause: pairs_table accepted any related table holding an identifier.
findings.fix: pairs_table needs a related table of two or three columns, at least two identifiers, no time column and a pair word in its names; with no data it is false.

findings.defect: Cleaning phrases routed to the matching kind.
findings.scenario: 'Predict churn; the export has some duplicate rows' was detected as a matching problem.
findings.cause: The kind's words included plain duplicate and dedup phrases.
findings.fix: Only phrases of matching records across sources or copies of bills; cleaning words removed.

findings.defect: The decision threshold was read from a coarse grid and refitted after the choice.
findings.scenario: Twenty true pairs in twenty thousand: the grid's best F1 was below the best of every distinct score, and the refit moved the threshold away from the one validated.
findings.cause: A fixed grid of thresholds and a refit after the choice.
findings.fix: Every distinct score is a candidate threshold; models are fitted on training pairs, thresholds set on validation, never refitted.

findings.defect: A forbidden or identifier column could be compared as a field.
findings.scenario: A solution comparing the bill id or the fraud label as a field was accepted.
findings.cause: check_solution did not refuse forbidden or identifier fields.
findings.fix: check_solution refuses an identifier compared, a forbidden column, no blocking and a wrong metric.

findings.defect: Known matches whose records were missing were dropped silently.
findings.scenario: The pairs table's two columns swapped gave pair F1 0 silently; float ids ('12.0') matched no record.
findings.cause: ids were compared as written and unfound matches were ignored.
findings.fix: ids normalised; more than 5% of the matches unfound raises with the hint to check the column order; a repeated id raises.

findings.defect: The certification counted the replica as passed when one seed passed and read the baselines' win without its interval.
findings.scenario: Seeds 1 and 2 below the trap's bars were hidden behind the count; a win by 0.005 counted.
findings.cause: run_kind aggregated before checking every seed; beats was a strict greater-than only.
findings.fix: The replica passes only when every seed passes; detection is the router's own choice; beats needs the difference's 90% interval above 0.
findings.test: python -m dclab_rnd.certify --kind matching (every seed read; the baselines' wins with their intervals)

findings.defect: The exact rule ignored the plan's exact links.
findings.scenario: The rule compared amount and time only and found no copy.
findings.cause: No flag field kind and no key fields.
findings.fix: A flag kind (either and both) and the key fields (items, returned_by_seller) the exact rule reads.

findings.defect: Nearest-neighbour blocking ran one way only.
findings.scenario: A copy whose original was not among its own ten neighbours, but which was among the original's, was never a candidate.
findings.cause: kNN from the left records to the right only.

findings.defect: The return-by-seller link's moment was not stated.
findings.scenario: The kind read a return made after the bill as if known when the bill was sold.
findings.cause: The moment said 'when a bill is sold'.
findings.fix: The moment is the end of a review period: each bill against the bills around it, with every return filed against it.
findings.test: the replica case's stated moment, read in the review

findings.defect: Records joined through a third record were not counted as matches.
findings.scenario: A, B and C with A~B and B~C: the pair A,C was a non-match in training.
findings.fix: Entities by union-find; every pair inside an entity is a match.

findings.defect: Block columns missing from a table failed deep in the run.
findings.scenario: A solution blocking on a column of the right table only crashed in candidates.
findings.cause: columns were checked only for fields.
findings.fix: Block columns of both tables are checked up front by columns_of and table_columns_of.

findings.defect: G4 failed on the copied bills: the holdout's F1 had no interval, so the gap to the folds could not be judged.
findings.scenario: The engine's final stage on seed 0: G4 back to the workflow with the gap 'unread'.
findings.cause: The matching machine wrote the holdout F1 without holdout_primary_metric_ci.
findings.fix: The F1's 95% interval from the entity bootstrap is written at the final stage.

findings.defect: The router's frozen schema limits moved with a new approach.
findings.scenario: test_core_contracts failed: the route schema's maxItems changed from the baseline.
findings.cause: MAX_NEEDS and MAX_CANDIDATES were computed from the approaches.
findings.fix: Frozen as constants (13, 16) the approaches must fit in.

measurements.name: the matching kind's certification (CRT-002, from committed code)
measurements.gate: the recipes' rule: a trap replica on every seed and two real datasets pass every criterion (detection by the router, traps, beating both baselines with the difference's 90% interval above zero, the code export, the same result with the model off)
measurements.result: the copied bills' pair F1 0.760, 0.702, 0.784 on seeds 0 to 2 (exact rule 0.011 to 0.012, one field 0 to 0.012); DBLP-ACM 0.983 (exact 0.901, one field 0.921); Abt-Buy 0.610 (exact 0.035, one field 0.550); every criterion passed
limits: The replica's known matches are every copy; the benchmarks are labelled in full.
Every holdout record is compared with every record: the bills' scores are lower than the first run's, which compared the holdout with itself.
Abt-Buy's win over one field is the narrowest (0.610 against 0.550).

outcome: DCLab matches records as its sixteenth kind, keeps a record and its matches on one side, says how many true pairs its blocking kept, and is certified on copied bills and two real benchmarks.
lessons: Before lowering a rule to meet a plan's wording, ask whether the data that meets the rule can be had.
A trap that a rule's count passes on one seed is not passed: read every seed.
Pair a test record with what a new record would meet in use, not with what is convenient to split.
risks: The kind has no dev or sealed journeys of its own yet, and no service export.
The router's pairs_table rule reads names (a pair word); a pairs table named otherwise is missed and the problem keeps its rare-event route.
